O’Halloran stood a round and then Farrington stood another round, Weathers protesting that the hospitality was too Irish.
After a while O’Halloran and Paddy Leonard came in and the story was repeated to them.
He knew where he would meet the boys: Leonard and O’Halloran and Nosey Flynn.
“Sh, sh!” said O’Halloran, observing the violent expression of Farrington’s face.

O’Halloran said that he and Leonard would go, but that Farrington wouldn’t go because he was a married man; and Farrington’s heavy dirty eyes leered at the company in token that he understood he was being chaffed.
